# Searching in Everything

Use the [search box](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#search_box) at the top of the Everything window to search for files and folders.

Type in a partial filename.

Files and folders matching your search will be instantly displayed in the [result list](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#result_list).

[A simple search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#simple)

[Combine simple searches](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#combine)

[Search drives and folders](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#path)

[Search options](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#options)

[Advanced Search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#advanced_search)

[Search Modifiers](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#modifiers)

[Search Functions](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#functions)

[Content Searching](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#content_searching)

[Finding duplicates](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#dupe)

[Filters](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#filters)

[Bookmarks](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#bookmarks)

[Macros](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#macros)

[Search History](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#history)

[Home search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#home)

[Search settings](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#settings)

[Regular Expressions](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#regex)

[Examples](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#examples)

[See also](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#see_also)

## A simple search

Type a partial word to instantly find files and folders with that word in the filename.

For example:

`invoice` = find files and folders with **invoice** in the filename

Use [wildcards](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#wildcards) to find files with a matching extension.

For example:

`*.pdf` = find only PDF files

Include a backslash (`\`) to search the full path.

For example:

`\downloads` = find files and folders in a Downloads folder

## Combine simple searches

Use a space to combine simple searches.

For example:

`\downloads invoice *.pdf` = find PDF files with **invoice** in the filename in a Downloads folder

Use a vertical bar (`|`) to search for either of the simple searches.

For example:

`\downloads|\documents invoice *.pdf` = find PDF files with **invoice** in the filename in either a Downloads or Documents folder

Use an exclamation mark (`!`) to exclude a simple search.

For example:

`\documents !draft *.docx` = find Microsoft Word files in a Documents folder without **draft** in the filename

Use the [Advanced Search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#advanced_search) from the **Search** menu to build more complex searches without having to remember the search syntax.

For a complete list of search operators and syntax rules, see [Search Syntax](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/).

## Search drives and folders

To limit the results to a single drive, search for the drive letter followed by a colon (`:`)

For example:

`d:` = find files and folders on your **D:** drive

To search multiple drives at once, separate the drive letters with a vertical bar (`|`)

For example:

`c:|e:` = find files and folders on your **C:** or **E:** drives

To exclude a drive from your search, prefix the drive letter with an exclamation mark (`!`)

For example:

`!e:` = hide files and folders on your **E:** drive

To search inside a specific folder, search for the folder path with a trailing backslash (`\`)

For example:

`C:\windows\media\` = find files and folders in **C:\\Windows\\Media**

A trailing backslash (`\`) specifies a folder.

Without the trailing backslash, the search can also match names that begin with the specified path.

For example:

`C:\windows\media` = can also match a file named **C:\\Windows\\Media2**

Use double quotes (`"`) around paths that contain spaces.

For example:

`"c:\program files\"` = find files and folders in **C:\\Program Files**

Without double quotes, the space separates the search into two simple searches:

`C:\Program Files` searches for **C:\\Program** in the full path and **Files** in the name.

## Search options

The [Search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu contains options for controlling how Everything searches.

Enabled search options are shown on the right side of the [status bar](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#status_bar).

Double-click a search option in the status bar to disable it.

_Match Case_Match uppercase and lowercase letters exactly.

_Match Diacritics_Match accent marks exactly.

_Match Whole Words_Match complete words instead of matching text within words.

_Match Path_Match against the full path instead of just the name.

_Match Prefix_Match only the beginning of words.

_Match Suffix_Match only the end of words.

_Ignore Punctuation_Ignore punctuation in filenames.

_Ignore White-space_Ignore whitespaces in filenames.

_Regular Expressions_Enable [Regular Expressions](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#regex) for advanced pattern matching.

_Everything__Audio__Compressed__Document__Executable__Folder__Image__Video_Search using the selected filter.

For more information, see [Filters](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#filters).

## Advanced Search

Use Advanced Search to build more complex searches without having to remember the search syntax.

![Everything Advanced Search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/Everything.Advanced.Search.png)

To show the advanced search dialog:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Search** menu, click **Advanced Search**.

## Search Modifiers

Search modifiers change how your search behaves.

They temporarily override search options set under the [Search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#options) menu.

For example:

`case:README` = finds files and folders with uppercase **README** in the filename without having to enable **Match Case** from the **Search** menu

For a complete list of modifiers, see [Search Modifiers](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/).

## Search Functions

Search functions find files and folders by [properties](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/properties/).

For example:

`size:>100mb` = instantly find files and folders larger than 100 MB

`date-modified:today` = instantly find files and folders modified today

`*.docx content:vanilla` = find Word documents containing **vanilla**

For a complete list of functions and syntax, see [Search Functions](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_functions/).

## Content Searching

Everything can search for specific text inside your files.

Standard text files are supported natively.

For other document types (such as Word documents or PDFs), Everything uses your system's installed [IFilters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFilter) to extract searchable text.

If no IFilter is available for a file type, Everything falls back to searching the file directly as text.

For example:

`*.pdf \downloads content:invoice` = find PDF files in the **Downloads** folder that contain the word **invoice**

`*.docx recipe content:garlic` = find Word documents with **recipe** in the filename and containing **garlic**

`ext:cpp;h;cs dm:thisyear content:TODO` = find source code files modified this year that contain the text **TODO**

Because file content is not indexed, content searches can be extremely slow.

For the best performance, combine content searches with other search filters (like file extensions, paths, or modified dates) to limit the number of files Everything needs to read.

For more information, see [content:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_functions/#content).

## Finding duplicates

Everything can quickly find files and folders with duplicate names, sizes, dates, and other properties.

Requires [Everything 1.5](https://www.voidtools.com/everything-1.5/)

To find duplicate results, right-click a column header and click **Find _<property>_ duplicates**.

For example:

Right-click the **Size** column header and click **Find Size duplicates**.

For more information, see [Finding Duplicates](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/find_duplicates/).

## Filters

Filters are saved searches that can be activated without changing the search in the search box.

Everything includes several default filters, such as **Audio** and **Video**.

Filters can be activated from the [Search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu, [filter bar](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#filters), or [filters sidebar](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#filters).

The active filter is shown on the right side of the [status bar](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#status_bar).

Double-click the active filter in the status bar to disable it.

To edit an existing filter:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Search** menu, click **Organize filters...**.
- Select a filter.
- Click **Edit**.

To add an extension to an existing default filter:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Search** menu, click **Organize filters...**.
- Select a filter.
- Click **Edit**.
- Add the extension to the end of the semicolon (`;`) separated extension list in the filter search.
- Click **OK**.

To create a new filter:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Search** menu, click **Add to filters...**.
- Type in a **Name**.
- Set the filter **Search**.
- Click **OK**.

To show the filter bar:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **View** menu, click **Filter bar**.

To move the filter bar:

- Right-click the filter bar and click **Move Filter Bar to Left/Right**.

Requires [Everything 1.5](https://www.voidtools.com/everything-1.5/)

To show the filter sidebar:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **View** menu, click **Filters**.

Requires [Everything 1.5](https://www.voidtools.com/everything-1.5/)

Filters can also be assigned [macros](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#macros) that are treated as the filter search text when used in the search box.

## Bookmarks

Bookmarks save the current search.

Opening a bookmark replaces the text in the search box and restores the saved settings.

Bookmarks can be opened from the [Bookmarks](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu or [Bookmarks sidebar](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#bookmarks).

Unlike [filters](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#filters), bookmarks replace the current search in the search box.

Bookmarks can also save the active filter, shown columns, sort order, view settings, and index settings.

To create a new bookmark from the current search:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Bookmarks** menu, click **Add to bookmarks...**.
- Type in a **Name**.
- Click **OK**.

To organize bookmarks:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Bookmarks** menu, click **Organize bookmarks...**.

To show the bookmarks sidebar:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **View** menu, click **Bookmarks**.

Requires [Everything 1.5](https://www.voidtools.com/everything-1.5/)

Bookmarks can also be assigned [macros](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#macros) that are treated as the bookmark search text when used in the search box.

## Macros

Macros are custom keywords followed by a colon (`:`) that are treated as the saved filter or bookmark search text.

For example, the default **Audio** filter uses the `audio` macro.

Searching for `audio:` in the search box is treated as the full search text from the **Audio** filter.

Macros make it easy to combine filters.

For example:

`audio:|video:` = find files matching either the **Audio** or **Video** filter.

To create a custom Bookmark macro:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Bookmarks** menu, click **Add to bookmarks...**.
- Type in a **Name**.
- Set a keyword for the **Macro** (for example: `mymacro`).
- Click **OK**.

Using `mymacro:` in the search box is treated as the search text defined in the bookmark.

Any search options, columns, or view settings saved in the bookmark are temporarily applied while `mymacro:` is in the search box.

Default filter macros for searching by file type:

- `audio:` = music and audio files
- `doc:` = documents, PDFs, and text files
- `exe:` = programs and installers
- `image:` = photos and graphics
- `video:` = movies and video clips
- `zip:` = ZIP files and archives

## Search History

Everything remembers your previous searches, previous session, recently closed tabs, and recently closed windows.

A search is added to the history when an action is performed on a result.

Recent searches can be accessed from the drop-down box to the right of the search box.

To find an older search:

- In **_Everything_**, from the [History](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu, click **Find Search History**.

To restore a previous session:

- In **_Everything_**, from the [History](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu, click **Restore Previous Session**.

To restore a previously closed tab:

- In **_Everything_**, from the [History](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu, under the **Recently Closed Tabs** submenu, click your tab.

To restore a previously closed window:

- In **_Everything_**, from the [History](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu, under the **Recently Closed Windows** submenu, click your window.

For more information, see [Search History](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_history/).

## Home search

The home search is the default search when you first open an Everything search window or tab.

The home search can also save the active filter, shown columns, sort order, view settings, and index settings.

To restore the home search:

- In **_Everything_**, from the [History](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu, click **Home**.

To change the home search settings:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Tools** menu, click **Options**.
- Click the [Home](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/options/#home) tab.
- Set the desired search options, search, filter, columns, sort order, view settings, and index settings.
- Click **OK**.

## Search settings

Configure search as you type, search box focus and selection, matching whole filename when using wildcards, and other search settings.

To manage your search settings:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Tools** menu, click **Options**.
- Click the **Search** tab on the left.

For more information, see [Options](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/options/#search).

## Regular Expressions

Regular expressions are a powerful way to search for patterns in filenames.

Everything uses Perl Compatible Regular Expressions (PCRE).

When regular expressions are enabled in the [Search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu, the normal Everything search syntax is disabled.

Search operators, wildcards, macros, modifiers, and functions are not supported.

To use regular expressions for part of a search, add the [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex) modifier before your search.

Standard Everything search syntax still works everywhere else.

For example:

`*.jpg regex:^IMG_\d+` = find JPG files starting with **IMG\_** followed by one or more digits

`*.txt regex:^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` = find TXT files starting with a date in YYYY-MM-DD format

Enclose the pattern in double quotes (`"`) when using spaces with the `regex:` search modifier.

For example:

`regex:" - \d\d - "` = find filenames containing two digits enclosed by spaces and a hyphen

Regular expression syntax:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| `a|b` | Matches a or b |
| `gr(a|e)y` | Matches gray or grey |
| `.` | Matches any single character |
| `[abc]` | Matches a single character a, b or c |
| `[^abc]` | Matches any single character except a, b or c |
| `[a-z]` | Matches a single character in the range a to z |
| `[a-zA-Z]` | Matches a single character in the range a to z or A to Z |
| `^` | Matches the start of the filename |
| `$` | Matches the end of the filename |
| `*` | Matches the preceding element zero or more times |
| `?` | Matches the preceding element zero or one times |
| `+` | Matches the preceding element one or more times |
| `{x}` | Matches the preceding element x times |
| `{x,}` | Matches the preceding element x or more times |
| `{x,y}` | Matches the preceding element between x and y times |
| `( )` | Defines a marked subexpression and captures the text it matches |
| `\` | Escapes a special character |

To view the regular expression syntax in Everything:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Help** menu, click **Regular Expression Syntax**.

The following examples demonstrate different ways to search in Everything, from simple searches to more advanced searches.

**Simple boolean searches**:

`abc 123` = find files and folders with **abc** and **123** in the filename

`abc|123` = find files and folders with **abc** or **123** in the filename

`!abc` = find files and folders without **abc** in the filename

**Simple wildcard searches**:

**File and folder searches**:

**Size searches**:

`size:10mb..50mb` = find files and folders between 10 MB and 50 MB

`size:<1mb` = find files and folders smaller than 1 MB

**Date modified searches**:

`dm:today` = find files and folders modified today

`dm:7days` = find files and folders modified in the last 7 days

`dm:2026-09-04` = find files and folders modified on 2026-09-04

`dm:>2022` = find files and folders modified after 2022

`dm:2025-07-01..2026-06-30` = find files and folders modified in the 2025-2026 financial year

Use the [search box](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#search_box) at the top of the Everything window to search for files and folders.

Type in a partial filename.

## A simple search

Type a partial word to instantly find files and folders with that word in the filename.

For example:

`invoice` = find files and folders with **invoice** in the filename

Use [wildcards](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#wildcards) to find files with a matching extension.

For example:

`*.pdf` = find only PDF files

Include a backslash (`\`) to search the full path.

For example:

`\downloads` = find files and folders in a Downloads folder

## Combine simple searches

Use a space to combine simple searches.

For example:

`\downloads invoice *.pdf` = find PDF files with **invoice** in the filename in a Downloads folder

Use a vertical bar (`|`) to search for either of the simple searches.

For example:

`\downloads|\documents invoice *.pdf` = find PDF files with **invoice** in the filename in either a Downloads or Documents folder

Use an exclamation mark (`!`) to exclude a simple search.

For example:

`\documents !draft *.docx` = find Microsoft Word files in a Documents folder without **draft** in the filename

Use the [Advanced Search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#advanced_search) from the **Search** menu to build more complex searches without having to remember the search syntax.

For a complete list of search operators and syntax rules, see [Search Syntax](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/).

## Search drives and folders

To limit the results to a single drive, search for the drive letter followed by a colon (`:`)

For example:

`d:` = find files and folders on your **D:** drive

To search multiple drives at once, separate the drive letters with a vertical bar (`|`)

For example:

`c:|e:` = find files and folders on your **C:** or **E:** drives

To exclude a drive from your search, prefix the drive letter with an exclamation mark (`!`)

For example:

`!e:` = hide files and folders on your **E:** drive

To search inside a specific folder, search for the folder path with a trailing backslash (`\`)

For example:

`C:\windows\media\` = find files and folders in **C:\\Windows\\Media**

A trailing backslash (`\`) specifies a folder.

Without the trailing backslash, the search can also match names that begin with the specified path.

For example:

`C:\windows\media` = can also match a file named **C:\\Windows\\Media2**

Use double quotes (`"`) around paths that contain spaces.

For example:

`"c:\program files\"` = find files and folders in **C:\\Program Files**

Without double quotes, the space separates the search into two simple searches:

`C:\Program Files` searches for **C:\\Program** in the full path and **Files** in the name.

The [Search](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#menu) menu contains options for controlling how Everything searches.

Enabled search options are shown on the right side of the [status bar](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/using_everything/#status_bar).

Double-click a search option in the status bar to disable it.

_Match Case_Match uppercase and lowercase letters exactly.

_Match Diacritics_Match accent marks exactly.

_Match Whole Words_Match complete words instead of matching text within words.

_Match Path_Match against the full path instead of just the name.

_Match Prefix_Match only the beginning of words.

_Match Suffix_Match only the end of words.

_Ignore Punctuation_Ignore punctuation in filenames.

_Ignore White-space_Ignore whitespaces in filenames.

_Regular Expressions_Enable [Regular Expressions](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#regex) for advanced pattern matching.

_Everything__Audio__Compressed__Document__Executable__Folder__Image__Video_Search using the selected filter.

## Content Searching

Everything can search for specific text inside your files.

Standard text files are supported natively.

For other document types (such as Word documents or PDFs), Everything uses your system's installed [IFilters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFilter) to extract searchable text.

If no IFilter is available for a file type, Everything falls back to searching the file directly as text.

For example:

`*.pdf \downloads content:invoice` = find PDF files in the **Downloads** folder that contain the word **invoice**

`*.docx recipe content:garlic` = find Word documents with **recipe** in the filename and containing **garlic**

Because file content is not indexed, content searches can be extremely slow.

For the best performance, combine content searches with other search filters (like file extensions, paths, or modified dates) to limit the number of files Everything needs to read.

# Search Syntax

An Everything search consists of one or more [search terms](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#syntax) joined by [search operators](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#operators).

Requires [Everything 1.5](https://www.voidtools.com/everything-1.5/)

[Syntax](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#syntax)

[Operators](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#operators)

[Wildcards](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#wildcards)

[Macros](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#macros)

[Character Entities](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#charentities)

[Filename Parts](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#parts)

[See also](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#see_also)

## Syntax

A search term specifies what to search.

The basic structure of a single search term is:

`[!][search-modifier:][search-function:]<text>`

!Optional [NOT operator](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#operators) to exclude the search term.

search-modifier:Optional [search modifiers](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/).

Multiple search modifiers may be specified to change how the search term is matched.

Search modifiers override default settings in the **Search** menu, allowing you to temporarily enable or disable matching options.

search-function:Optional [search function](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_functions/) to search a specific property, such as a date or size.

textSearch text or a value interpreted by the search function.

Literal text without a search function matches file and folder names.

If **Match Path** is enabled in the **Search** menu, literal text matches against the full path instead.

For example:

`abc` = matches filenames containing abc

`path:abc` = matches full paths containing abc

`date-modified:today` = matches files and folders modified today

`case:extension:JPG` = matches files with an extension containing uppercase JPG

`!abc` = excludes filenames containing abc

Search terms can be combined with [search operators](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#operators) to create more complex search expressions.

`<search-term> <operator> <search-term> ...`

For example:

`abc 123` = matches filenames containing both `abc` AND `123`

`*.jpg | *.png` = matches files with a `jpg` OR `png` extension

To view the search syntax in Everything:

- In **_Everything_**, from the **Help** menu, click **Search Syntax**.

## Operators

Operators combine [search terms](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#syntax) and control how they are evaluated.

_space_**AND** search terms together.

For example:

`abc 123` = matches `abc` AND `123`

\|**OR** search terms together.

Spaces immediately before or after `|` are ignored.

For example:

`abc|123` = matches `abc` OR `123`

`abc | 123` = matches `abc` OR `123`

!**NOT** a search term.

The search term that immediately follows is excluded.

For example:

`!abc` = matches NOT `abc`

< >**Group** search terms together to change the evaluation order.

For example:

`!<abc 123>` = matches NOT (`abc` AND `123`)

" "**Quote** search text.

Treats everything inside the quotes (including operators) as plain text.

For example:

`"C:\Program Files"` = matches the text: `C:\Program Files`

By default, OR is evaluated before AND.

For example:

`apple banana | orange` = matches `apple` AND (`banana` OR `orange`)

Use grouping `< >` to change the evaluation order.

For example:

`<apple banana> | orange` = matches (`apple` AND `banana`) OR `orange`

Operator precedence can be changed in the [Search Options](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/options/#operator_precedence).

## Wildcards

The following wildcards can be used in Everything searches:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| \* | Matches zero or more characters (except `\`) |
| \*\* | Matches zero or more characters |
| ? | Matches one character (except `\`) |

The whole filename is matched when using wildcards.

For example:

`*.mp3` = matches mp3 files

`foo*` = matches filenames starting with foo

`*foo*` = matches filenames containing foo

`stem:*bar` = matches filenames ending with bar (ignoring extension)

## Macros

The following macros can be used in Everything searches:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| audio: | Matches audio files. |
| doc: | Matches document files. |
| exe: | Matches executable files. |
| image: | Matches image files. |
| video: | Matches video files. |
| zip: | Matches compressed files. |

For example:

`audio:` = matches audio files

`audio:|video:` = matches audio or video files

Custom macros can be defined.

For more information, see [Macros](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/searching/#macros).

## Character Entities

The following character entities can be used in Everything searches:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| &sp: | Literal space (``) |
| &vert: | Literal vertical line (`|`) |
| &excl: | Literal exclamation mark (`!`) |
| &lt: | Literal less than (`<`) |
| &gt: | Literal greater than (`>`) |
| &quot: | Literal double quote (`"`) |
| &#<n>: | Literal Unicode character <n> in decimal. |
| &#x<n>: | Literal Unicode character <n> in hexadecimal. |

For example:

`C:\Program&sp:Files` = match files/folders in `C:\Program files`

`&excl:readme.txt` = match filenames containing `!readme.txt`

`content:&quot:foo&quot:` = match file content containing `"foo"`

`diacritics:&#xad:` = match filenames containing a soft hyphen (`-`)

[Character Entities](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=65789#p65789)

## Filename parts

The following filename parts describe the different components of a filename in Everything:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Full Path | `C:\folder\file.txt` |
| Name | `file.txt` |
| Path | `C:\folder` |
| Stem | `file` |
| Extension | `txt` |

# Search Modifiers

Search modifiers control how [search terms](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#syntax) are parsed and matched.

They can be used to enable features such as case-sensitive matching, whole-word matching, regular expressions, full path matching and many other search behaviors.

If no search modifiers are specified, Everything performs a partial filename search based on the current search settings.

Requires [Everything 1.5](https://www.voidtools.com/everything-1.5/)

## Syntax

Search modifiers are applied to a [single search term](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#syntax):

`search-modifier:[search-function:]<text>`

search-modifier:The search modifier name.

Multiple search modifiers may be specified to change how the search term is matched.

Search modifiers override default settings in the **Search** menu, allowing you to temporarily enable or disable matching options.

search-function:Optional [search function](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_functions/) to search a specific property, such as a date or size.

textSearch text or a value interpreted by the search function.

Search text without a search function matches against file and folder names.

If **Match Path** is enabled in the **Search** menu, search text matches against the full path instead.

Examples:

`case:ABC` = find files and folders whose filename contains **ABC** with case-sensitive matching

`len:album:>20` = find files where the album length is longer than **20** characters

`regex:^\d\d\d\d` = find files and folders whose filename starts with 4 digits

`regex:content:^\d\d\d\d` = find files where the content starts with 4 digits

`folder:case:wholewords:path:FOO` = find folders whose full path contains the whole word **FOO** with case-sensitive matching

Search modifiers can be disabled by prefixing them with: `no-`

For example, if **Match Path** is enabled under the **Search** menu, use `no-path:` to disable full path matching:

`no-path:abc`

Use a `*` suffix on a search modifier to treat the remainder of the search as plain text.

No further parsing is performed.

For example, to treat the remainder of the search as plain text with regex:

`regex*:^foo bar$` = the space is treated as plain text, not as the AND operator

Prefix a search modifier with `::` to explicitly specify built-in scope, bypassing user-defined overrides.

For example, to refer to the built-in case search modifier:

`::case:`

Prefix a search modifier with ? to enable it globally for the remainder of the search.

The search modifier does not need to be attached to a term.

For example, to enable case-sensitive matching for the remainder of the search:

`?case: FOO BAR` is the same as `case:FOO case:BAR`

Search modifiers can be applied to `< >` groups.

For example:

`case:<FOO BAR>` is the same as `case:FOO case:BAR`

Hyphens (`-`) in search modifiers can be omitted.

For example:

`no-whole-words:` is the same as `nowholewords:`

## All Modifiers

all-strings:Match all strings in a multi-string value.

For example:

`all-strings:author:john;"jane doe"`

Default: match any string value.

and-filter:AND this filter when multiple filters are selected.

Use in a filter search definition.

`and-filter:` is global and applies to the entire filter.

`and-filter:` has no effect on the search itself.

For example:

`and-filter: d:|e:`

`and-filter: !c:\windows\`

Default: OR multiple filters.

See also: [or-filter:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#or-filter)

and-precedence:Makes AND evaluate before OR when parsing search expressions.

For example:

`?and-precedence: sonic tails | mario luigi` =\> (sonic tails) \| (mario luigi)

Default: OR > AND. (see Tools -> Options -> Search -> Operator precedence setting)

See also: [?or-precedence:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#or-precedence)

binary:Treat the search and file content as a byte stream.

For example:

`binary:content:\x00\x00\x01\x10`

`binary:content:abc123`

ASCII text is supported.

Use `\x00` \- `\xff` to specify a byte value in hex.

Default: Disabled.

case:no-case:Enables or disables case-sensitive matching.

For example:

`case:WINDOWS`

`no-case:WINDOWS`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Match Case** setting under the **Search** menu)

diacritics:no-diacritics:Match or ignore accent marks.

For example:

`diacritics:"Déjà Vu"`

`no-diacritics:"Deja Vu"`

Aliases: `diac:`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Match Diacritics** setting under the **Search** menu)

dot-all:When enabled, regular expression `.` will match all characters.

When disabled, regular expression `.` will match all characters except new lines.

For example:

`dotall:regex:content:"line 1.*line 2"`

`regex:content:"(?s)line 1.*line 2"`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

each-line:Match each line or match the entire content.

If enabled, searching stops on the first line matched.

For example:

`eachline:content:<a b>` (find a and b on the same line)

`eachline:content:<a b c d|e|f !g !h !i>`

Default: Disabled. (match the entire content)

end-with:Match the end of filenames.

For example:

`endwith:hosts`

Aliases: `$:`

Default: Disabled.

no-fast-regex:Disable regex optimization.

Regex optimizations will need to be disabled if you would like to use the regex match 0 property without using a special character in your regex pattern.

For example:

`no-fast-regex:regex:abc123 regexmatch0:123`

Default: Enabled.

file:folder:Match files or folders only.

For example:

`folder:music`

`file: .mp3`

Default: Match files and folders.

global:When enabled, find all occurrences of the regular expression.

When disabled, find only the first occurrence.

If no group capture is specified, the entire match is captured.

For example:

`global:regex:\d+`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

hex:Convert 2 character hex codes into a single byte and treats the search and file content as a byte stream.

For example:

`hex:48656C6C6F`

`hex:startwith:content:89504E47` = matches PNG file signatures

Default: Disabled.

hex-to-number:Compare a filename or property value in hex as an integer.

For example:

`hex-to-number:0x1000..0x2000`

Default: Disabled.

no-highlight:Disable highlighting for this term.

For example:

`no-highlight:path:foo`

Default: Highlight the search term.

from-disk:Search properties and content from disk (not from the index).

For example:

`fromdisk:length:>5m`

Default: Search indexed properties only. If the property is not included in the index, search the property from disk.

len:Search for the length of the filename or property value in UTF-16 characters.

For example:

`len:>20`

`len:5..10`

`path:len:>259`

`len:3`

Default: Disabled.

menu-break:Show this filter or bookmark in a new menu column in context menus.

Use in a filter or bookmark search definition.

`menu-break:` is global and applies to the entire filter or bookmark.

`menu-break:` has no effect on the search itself.

For example:

`menu-break:`

Default: Show the filter or bookmark in one long context menu.

menu-separator:Show this filter or bookmark as a menu separator in context menus.

Use in a filter or bookmark search definition.

`menu-separator:` is global and applies to the entire filter or bookmark.

`menu-separator:` has no effect on the search itself.

For example:

`menu-separator:`

Default: Show filter by name.

metric:no-metric:Use the metric size standard.

For example:

`metric:size:1kb` = `size:1000`

Default: JEDEC. (see Tools -> Options -> Size Standard setting)

multi-line:Controls how ^ and $ behave in regex searches.

When enabled, ^ and $ match the start and end of each line.

When disabled, ^ and $ match the start and end of the entire text.

For example:

`multiline:regex:content:"^A line of text$"`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

multi-string:no-multi-string:Treats semicolon (`;`) separated property values as a list of individual strings.

When enabled, matching is applied to each item in the list separately.

When disabled, the entire value is treated as a single string.

For example:

`multistring:regex:content:"^An item in a list$"`

`nomultistring:zipfilename:"abc.txt;123.txt"`

Default: Enabled for properties that support multiple values. Otherwise disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

See also: [all-strings:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#all-strings)

no-!:Disable the not operator (`!`).

For example:

`no-!:!readme.txt`

Default: Allow the not operator (`!`).

or-filter:OR this filter when multiple filters are selected.

Use in a filter search definition.

`or-filter:` is global and applies to the entire filter.

`or-filter:` has no effect on the search itself.

For example:

`or-filter: ext:mp3;jpg`

Default: OR multiple filters.

See also: [and-filter:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#and-filter)

or-precedence:Makes OR evaluate before AND when parsing search expressions.

For example:

`?or-precedence: sonic tails | mario luigi` =\> sonic (tails \| mario) luigi

Default: OR > AND. (see Tools -> Options -> Search -> Operator precedence setting)

See also: [?and-precedence:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#and-precedence)

path:no-path:Enables or disables matching against the full path.

When enabled (`path:`), searches are performed on the full path and name.

When disabled (`no-path:`), searches are performed on the name only.

For example:

`path:system32 hosts`

Aliases: `\:`

Default: Use the **Match Path** setting under the **Search** menu.

Use the [path-part:](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=10176#pathpart) search function to search the path part only.

pinyin:no-pinyin:Match Chinese characters with QuanPin Pinyin.

For example:

`pinyin:nihao` = matches: 你好

Aliases: `py:`

Default: Use Tools -> Options -> Advanced -> pinyin setting. (disabled by default)

See also: [pinyin\_type](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=9994#pinyin_type)

See also: [pinyin-jian:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin-jian)

See also: [pinyin-quan:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin-quan)

pinyin-jian:Match Chinese characters with Single Character Pinyin.

For example:

`pinyin-jian:nh` = matches: 你好

Aliases: `pyj:`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [pinyin:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin)

See also: [pinyin-quan:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin-quan)

pinyin-quan:Match Chinese characters with QuanPin Pinyin.

For example:

`pinyin-quan:nihao` = matches: 你好

Aliases: `pyq:`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [pinyin-jian:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin-jian)

See also: [pinyin:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin)

prefix:no-prefix:Enables or disables matching the start of words.

For example:

`prefix:ever`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Prefix** setting under the **Search** menu)

ignore-punctuation:no-ignore-punctuation:Controls whether punctuation in filenames or property values is ignored.

For example:

`ignore-punctuation:spiderman` = matches `spider-man`

Aliases: `nopunc:`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Ignore Punctuation** setting under the **Search** menu)

See also: [ignore\_punctuation\_type](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=9994#ignore_punctuation_type)

regex:Enables regular expressions.

When enabled, the search term parser will eat all `|` characters.

Use `regex*:` (or `regex:function*:`) to treat the remainder of the search as plain text.

For example:

`regex:content:^foo`

`regex:content:gr(a|e)y`

`regex:content*:abc 123 "text in quotes"`

`case:regex:content:^FOO`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Regular Expressions** setting under the **Search** menu)

See also: [dot-all:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#dot-all)

See also: [global:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#global)

See also: [multi-line:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#multi-line)

See also: [ungreedy:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#ungreedy)

enable-result-omissions:disable-result-omissions:Enables or disables [result omissions](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/result_omissions/) globally.

Default: Disabled. (see the Enable Result Omissions setting under the Index menu)

no-reorder:Disables search term reordering.

When enabled, search terms are reordered from fastest to slowest.

For example:

`noreorder:content:^foo bar.txt`

Default: Enabled.

search-current-results:no-search-current-results:Enables or disables searching within the current results.

Everything will search within the current results when possible to improve performance.

Use `no-search-current-results:` to perform a full re-search.

Use `search-current-results:` to force Everything to search the current results.

For example:

`no-search-current-results: dm:5mins`

Default: Enabled.

soundex:Match files by SQL soundex.

The prefix is matched.

Combine with [whole-words:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#whole-words) to match whole words.

Only A-Z, a-z letters are currently supported.

For example:

`soundex:david`

`soundex:artist:michael`

Default: Disabled.

star-all:Controls whether wildcard `*` matches path separators.

When enabled, `*` matches all characters.

When disabled, `*` matches all characters except `\` and `/`.

For example:

`starall:c:*abc.txt`

Default: Disabled. (see Tools -> Options -> Advanced -> [wildcards\_star\_all](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?f=12&t=9994#wildcards_star_all))

start-with:Matches only the start of a filename or property value.

For example:

`startwith:ever`

Aliases: `^:`

Default: Disabled.

no-substitute:Disables property substitution.

When enabled, `$property:` is replaced with the value of the specified property.

For example:

`stem:$extension:` = matches files that have the extension in the stem. (eg: `txt.txt`)

`no-substitute:$extension:` = finds the plain text `$extension:` in the filename

Default: Enabled for filenames and filename-like property values. Otherwise disabled.

suffix:no-suffix:Enables or disables matching the end of words.

For example:

`suffix:hosts`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Suffix** setting under the **Search** menu)

enable-temp-result-omissions:disable-temp-result-omissions:Enables or disables [temporary result omissions](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/result_omissions/) globally.

Default: Disabled. (see the Enable Temporary Result Omissions setting under the Index menu)

to-integer:Compare a filename or property value as an integer.

For example:

`to-integer:album:>10`

Default: Disabled.

to-number:Compare a filename or property value as a real number.

For example:

`to-number:album:>1.5`

Aliases: `#:`

Default: Disabled.

to-string:Compare a property value as text.

For example:

`tostring:date-modified:/02/`

`regex:tostring:date-modified:^201`

Default: Disabled.

ungreedy:When enabled, regex quantifiers default to ungreedy (lazy) matching.

When disabled, regex quantifiers default to greedy matching.

For example:

`ungreedy:regex:(.*)` is the same as `regex:(.*?)`

`ungreedy:regex:(.*?)` is the same as `regex:(.*)`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

whole:Matches the whole filename or property value.

For example:

`whole:hosts`

Aliases: `whole-filename:``wfn:``entire:`

Default: Disabled.

ignore-whitespace:no-ignore-whitespace:Controls whether whitespace in filenames or property values is ignored.

For example:

`ignore-whitespace:spiderman` matches `spider man`

Aliases: `nows:`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Ignore White-Space** setting under the **Search** menu)

whole-words:no-whole-words:Enables or disables whole word matching.

For example:

`whole-words:foo`

Aliases: `ww:`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Match Whole Words** setting under the **Search** menu)

wildcards:no-wildcards:Enables extended wildcard matching or disables wildcard matching.

By default, `*` and `?` are treated as filename wildcards (for example `*.mp3`).

When enabled, `wildcards:` uses extended wildcard syntax for advanced search patterns.

Use `wildcards*:` (or `wildcards:function*:`) to treat the remainder of the search as plain text.

Use `no-wildcards:` to disable all wildcard matching, allowing literal `*` and `?` characters to be searched.

Use `&quest:` for `?` and `&ast:` for `*` to escape filename wildcard characters.

Escaping a filename wildcard disables filename wildcard matching.

`*` = matches zero or more characters

`?` = matches any single character

`#` = matches any single digit (`0`-`9`)

`[ ]` = matches any character in the set

`[! ]` = matches any character not in the set

`\` = escapes the next character (supports C-style escape sequences)

For example:

`wildcards:####*`

`wildcards:[a-m]*`

`wildcards:content:foo*`

`wildcards:content*:a b c*`

`wildcards:*\x0D\x0A`

`no-wildcards:?`

Default:

Filename wildcards: Enabled. (see Tools -> Options -> Advanced -> [wildcards](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?f=12&t=9994#wildcards))

Extended wildcards: Disabled.

# Search Modifiers

Search modifiers control how [search terms](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#syntax) are parsed and matched.

They can be used to enable features such as case-sensitive matching, whole-word matching, regular expressions, full path matching and many other search behaviors.

If no search modifiers are specified, Everything performs a partial filename search based on the current search settings.

Requires [Everything 1.5](https://www.voidtools.com/everything-1.5/)

[Syntax](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#syntax)

## Syntax

Search modifiers are applied to a [single search term](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_syntax/#syntax):

`search-modifier:[search-function:]<text>`

search-modifier:The search modifier name.

Multiple search modifiers may be specified to change how the search term is matched.

Search modifiers override default settings in the **Search** menu, allowing you to temporarily enable or disable matching options.

search-function:Optional [search function](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_functions/) to search a specific property, such as a date or size.

textSearch text or a value interpreted by the search function.

Search text without a search function matches against file and folder names.

If **Match Path** is enabled in the **Search** menu, search text matches against the full path instead.

Examples:

`case:ABC` = find files and folders whose filename contains **ABC** with case-sensitive matching

`len:album:>20` = find files where the album length is longer than **20** characters

`regex:^\d\d\d\d` = find files and folders whose filename starts with 4 digits

`regex:content:^\d\d\d\d` = find files where the content starts with 4 digits

`folder:case:wholewords:path:FOO` = find folders whose full path contains the whole word **FOO** with case-sensitive matching

Search modifiers can be disabled by prefixing them with: `no-`

For example, if **Match Path** is enabled under the **Search** menu, use `no-path:` to disable full path matching:

`no-path:abc`

Use a `*` suffix on a search modifier to treat the remainder of the search as plain text.

No further parsing is performed.

For example, to treat the remainder of the search as plain text with regex:

`regex*:^foo bar$` = the space is treated as plain text, not as the AND operator

Prefix a search modifier with `::` to explicitly specify built-in scope, bypassing user-defined overrides.

For example, to refer to the built-in case search modifier:

`::case:`

Prefix a search modifier with ? to enable it globally for the remainder of the search.

The search modifier does not need to be attached to a term.

For example, to enable case-sensitive matching for the remainder of the search:

`?case: FOO BAR` is the same as `case:FOO case:BAR`

Search modifiers can be applied to `< >` groups.

For example:

`case:<FOO BAR>` is the same as `case:FOO case:BAR`

Hyphens (`-`) in search modifiers can be omitted.

For example:

`no-whole-words:` is the same as `nowholewords:`

## All Modifiers

all-strings:Match all strings in a multi-string value.

For example:

`all-strings:author:john;"jane doe"`

Default: match any string value.

and-filter:AND this filter when multiple filters are selected.

Use in a filter search definition.

`and-filter:` is global and applies to the entire filter.

`and-filter:` has no effect on the search itself.

For example:

`and-filter: d:|e:`

`and-filter: !c:\windows\`

Default: OR multiple filters.

See also: [or-filter:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#or-filter)

and-precedence:Makes AND evaluate before OR when parsing search expressions.

For example:

`?and-precedence: sonic tails | mario luigi` =\> (sonic tails) \| (mario luigi)

Default: OR > AND. (see Tools -> Options -> Search -> Operator precedence setting)

See also: [?or-precedence:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#or-precedence)

binary:Treat the search and file content as a byte stream.

For example:

`binary:content:\x00\x00\x01\x10`

`binary:content:abc123`

ASCII text is supported.

Use `\x00` \- `\xff` to specify a byte value in hex.

Default: Disabled.

case:no-case:Enables or disables case-sensitive matching.

For example:

`case:WINDOWS`

`no-case:WINDOWS`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Match Case** setting under the **Search** menu)

diacritics:no-diacritics:Match or ignore accent marks.

For example:

`diacritics:"Déjà Vu"`

`no-diacritics:"Deja Vu"`

Aliases: `diac:`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Match Diacritics** setting under the **Search** menu)

dot-all:When enabled, regular expression `.` will match all characters.

When disabled, regular expression `.` will match all characters except new lines.

For example:

`dotall:regex:content:"line 1.*line 2"`

`regex:content:"(?s)line 1.*line 2"`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

each-line:Match each line or match the entire content.

If enabled, searching stops on the first line matched.

For example:

`eachline:content:<a b>` (find a and b on the same line)

`eachline:content:<a b c d|e|f !g !h !i>`

Default: Disabled. (match the entire content)

end-with:Match the end of filenames.

For example:

`endwith:hosts`

Aliases: `$:`

Default: Disabled.

no-fast-regex:Disable regex optimization.

Regex optimizations will need to be disabled if you would like to use the regex match 0 property without using a special character in your regex pattern.

For example:

`no-fast-regex:regex:abc123 regexmatch0:123`

Default: Enabled.

file:folder:Match files or folders only.

For example:

`folder:music`

`file: .mp3`

Default: Match files and folders.

global:When enabled, find all occurrences of the regular expression.

When disabled, find only the first occurrence.

If no group capture is specified, the entire match is captured.

For example:

`global:regex:\d+`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

hex:Convert 2 character hex codes into a single byte and treats the search and file content as a byte stream.

For example:

`hex:48656C6C6F`

`hex:startwith:content:89504E47` = matches PNG file signatures

Default: Disabled.

hex-to-number:Compare a filename or property value in hex as an integer.

For example:

`hex-to-number:0x1000..0x2000`

Default: Disabled.

no-highlight:Disable highlighting for this term.

For example:

`no-highlight:path:foo`

Default: Highlight the search term.

from-disk:Search properties and content from disk (not from the index).

For example:

`fromdisk:length:>5m`

Default: Search indexed properties only. If the property is not included in the index, search the property from disk.

len:Search for the length of the filename or property value in UTF-16 characters.

For example:

`len:>20`

`len:5..10`

`path:len:>259`

`len:3`

Default: Disabled.

menu-break:Show this filter or bookmark in a new menu column in context menus.

Use in a filter or bookmark search definition.

`menu-break:` is global and applies to the entire filter or bookmark.

`menu-break:` has no effect on the search itself.

For example:

`menu-break:`

Default: Show the filter or bookmark in one long context menu.

menu-separator:Show this filter or bookmark as a menu separator in context menus.

Use in a filter or bookmark search definition.

`menu-separator:` is global and applies to the entire filter or bookmark.

`menu-separator:` has no effect on the search itself.

For example:

`menu-separator:`

Default: Show filter by name.

metric:no-metric:Use the metric size standard.

For example:

`metric:size:1kb` = `size:1000`

Default: JEDEC. (see Tools -> Options -> Size Standard setting)

multi-line:Controls how ^ and $ behave in regex searches.

When enabled, ^ and $ match the start and end of each line.

When disabled, ^ and $ match the start and end of the entire text.

For example:

`multiline:regex:content:"^A line of text$"`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

multi-string:no-multi-string:Treats semicolon (`;`) separated property values as a list of individual strings.

When enabled, matching is applied to each item in the list separately.

When disabled, the entire value is treated as a single string.

For example:

`multistring:regex:content:"^An item in a list$"`

`nomultistring:zipfilename:"abc.txt;123.txt"`

Default: Enabled for properties that support multiple values. Otherwise disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

See also: [all-strings:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#all-strings)

no-!:Disable the not operator (`!`).

For example:

`no-!:!readme.txt`

Default: Allow the not operator (`!`).

or-filter:OR this filter when multiple filters are selected.

Use in a filter search definition.

`or-filter:` is global and applies to the entire filter.

`or-filter:` has no effect on the search itself.

For example:

`or-filter: ext:mp3;jpg`

Default: OR multiple filters.

See also: [and-filter:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#and-filter)

or-precedence:Makes OR evaluate before AND when parsing search expressions.

For example:

`?or-precedence: sonic tails | mario luigi` =\> sonic (tails \| mario) luigi

Default: OR > AND. (see Tools -> Options -> Search -> Operator precedence setting)

See also: [?and-precedence:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#and-precedence)

path:no-path:Enables or disables matching against the full path.

When enabled (`path:`), searches are performed on the full path and name.

When disabled (`no-path:`), searches are performed on the name only.

For example:

`path:system32 hosts`

Aliases: `\:`

Default: Use the **Match Path** setting under the **Search** menu.

Use the [path-part:](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=10176#pathpart) search function to search the path part only.

pinyin:no-pinyin:Match Chinese characters with QuanPin Pinyin.

For example:

`pinyin:nihao` = matches: 你好

Aliases: `py:`

Default: Use Tools -> Options -> Advanced -> pinyin setting. (disabled by default)

See also: [pinyin\_type](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=9994#pinyin_type)

See also: [pinyin-jian:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin-jian)

See also: [pinyin-quan:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin-quan)

pinyin-jian:Match Chinese characters with Single Character Pinyin.

For example:

`pinyin-jian:nh` = matches: 你好

Aliases: `pyj:`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [pinyin:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin)

See also: [pinyin-quan:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin-quan)

pinyin-quan:Match Chinese characters with QuanPin Pinyin.

For example:

`pinyin-quan:nihao` = matches: 你好

Aliases: `pyq:`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [pinyin-jian:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin-jian)

See also: [pinyin:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#pinyin)

prefix:no-prefix:Enables or disables matching the start of words.

For example:

`prefix:ever`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Prefix** setting under the **Search** menu)

ignore-punctuation:no-ignore-punctuation:Controls whether punctuation in filenames or property values is ignored.

For example:

`ignore-punctuation:spiderman` = matches `spider-man`

Aliases: `nopunc:`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Ignore Punctuation** setting under the **Search** menu)

See also: [ignore\_punctuation\_type](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=9994#ignore_punctuation_type)

regex:Enables regular expressions.

When enabled, the search term parser will eat all `|` characters.

Use `regex*:` (or `regex:function*:`) to treat the remainder of the search as plain text.

For example:

`regex:content:^foo`

`regex:content:gr(a|e)y`

`regex:content*:abc 123 "text in quotes"`

`case:regex:content:^FOO`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Regular Expressions** setting under the **Search** menu)

See also: [dot-all:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#dot-all)

See also: [global:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#global)

See also: [multi-line:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#multi-line)

See also: [ungreedy:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#ungreedy)

enable-result-omissions:disable-result-omissions:Enables or disables [result omissions](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/result_omissions/) globally.

Default: Disabled. (see the Enable Result Omissions setting under the Index menu)

no-reorder:Disables search term reordering.

When enabled, search terms are reordered from fastest to slowest.

For example:

`noreorder:content:^foo bar.txt`

Default: Enabled.

search-current-results:no-search-current-results:Enables or disables searching within the current results.

Everything will search within the current results when possible to improve performance.

Use `no-search-current-results:` to perform a full re-search.

Use `search-current-results:` to force Everything to search the current results.

For example:

`no-search-current-results: dm:5mins`

Default: Enabled.

soundex:Match files by SQL soundex.

The prefix is matched.

Combine with [whole-words:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#whole-words) to match whole words.

Only A-Z, a-z letters are currently supported.

For example:

`soundex:david`

`soundex:artist:michael`

Default: Disabled.

star-all:Controls whether wildcard `*` matches path separators.

When enabled, `*` matches all characters.

When disabled, `*` matches all characters except `\` and `/`.

For example:

`starall:c:*abc.txt`

Default: Disabled. (see Tools -> Options -> Advanced -> [wildcards\_star\_all](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?f=12&t=9994#wildcards_star_all))

start-with:Matches only the start of a filename or property value.

For example:

`startwith:ever`

Aliases: `^:`

Default: Disabled.

no-substitute:Disables property substitution.

When enabled, `$property:` is replaced with the value of the specified property.

For example:

`stem:$extension:` = matches files that have the extension in the stem. (eg: `txt.txt`)

`no-substitute:$extension:` = finds the plain text `$extension:` in the filename

Default: Enabled for filenames and filename-like property values. Otherwise disabled.

suffix:no-suffix:Enables or disables matching the end of words.

For example:

`suffix:hosts`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Suffix** setting under the **Search** menu)

enable-temp-result-omissions:disable-temp-result-omissions:Enables or disables [temporary result omissions](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/result_omissions/) globally.

Default: Disabled. (see the Enable Temporary Result Omissions setting under the Index menu)

to-integer:Compare a filename or property value as an integer.

For example:

`to-integer:album:>10`

Default: Disabled.

to-number:Compare a filename or property value as a real number.

For example:

`to-number:album:>1.5`

Aliases: `#:`

Default: Disabled.

to-string:Compare a property value as text.

For example:

`tostring:date-modified:/02/`

`regex:tostring:date-modified:^201`

Default: Disabled.

ungreedy:When enabled, regex quantifiers default to ungreedy (lazy) matching.

When disabled, regex quantifiers default to greedy matching.

For example:

`ungreedy:regex:(.*)` is the same as `regex:(.*?)`

`ungreedy:regex:(.*?)` is the same as `regex:(.*)`

Default: Disabled.

See also: [regex:](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/search_modifiers/#regex)

whole:Matches the whole filename or property value.

For example:

`whole:hosts`

Aliases: `whole-filename:``wfn:``entire:`

Default: Disabled.

ignore-whitespace:no-ignore-whitespace:Controls whether whitespace in filenames or property values is ignored.

For example:

`ignore-whitespace:spiderman` matches `spider man`

Aliases: `nows:`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Ignore White-Space** setting under the **Search** menu)

whole-words:no-whole-words:Enables or disables whole word matching.

For example:

`whole-words:foo`

Aliases: `ww:`

Default: Disabled. (see the **Match Whole Words** setting under the **Search** menu)

wildcards:no-wildcards:Enables extended wildcard matching or disables wildcard matching.

By default, `*` and `?` are treated as filename wildcards (for example `*.mp3`).

When enabled, `wildcards:` uses extended wildcard syntax for advanced search patterns.

Use `wildcards*:` (or `wildcards:function*:`) to treat the remainder of the search as plain text.

Use `no-wildcards:` to disable all wildcard matching, allowing literal `*` and `?` characters to be searched.

Use `&quest:` for `?` and `&ast:` for `*` to escape filename wildcard characters.

Escaping a filename wildcard disables filename wildcard matching.

`*` = matches zero or more characters

`?` = matches any single character

`#` = matches any single digit (`0`-`9`)

`[ ]` = matches any character in the set

`[! ]` = matches any character not in the set

`\` = escapes the next character (supports C-style escape sequences)

For example:

`wildcards:####*`

`wildcards:[a-m]*`

`wildcards:content:foo*`

`wildcards:content*:a b c*`

`wildcards:*\x0D\x0A`

`no-wildcards:?`

Default:

Filename wildcards: Enabled. (see Tools -> Options -> Advanced -> [wildcards](https://www.voidtools.com/forum/viewtopic.php?f=12&t=9994#wildcards))

Extended wildcards: Disabled.

# Results

The result list shows the file and folders matches for the current search.

Right click a file or folder to perform an action, such as open, cut, copy, delete, rename or properties.

## Thumbnails

![Everything Thumbnails](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/Everything.Thumbnails.png)

To show results in thumbnail view:

- In " **_Everything_**", from the **View** menu, click **Medium Thumbnails**, **Large Thumbnails** or **Extra Large Thumbnails**.

-or-

- In " **_Everything_**", Press and hold the Ctrl key and use the mouse wheel to change the view from Details to Extra Large Thumbnails.

## Preview

![Everything Preview](https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/Everything.Preview.png)

To show the preview pane:

- In " **_Everything_**", from the **View** menu, check **Preview**.

Click and drag the divider to resize the preview pane.

## Hide results when the search is empty

All files and folders are found when the search is empty. To hide the results when the search is empty:

- In " **_Everything_**", from the **Tools** menu, click **Options**.
- Check **Hide results when the search is empty**.
- Click **OK**.

## Keep selection

When you change the search in Everything, the current selection is cleared.

To keep the selection after changing the search:

- In " **_Everything_**", from the **Tools** menu, click **Options**.
- Click the **Results** tab.
- Uncheck the **Clear selection on search**.
- Click **OK**.

## Jump to

Type in the start of a filename to jump to it.

The jump to text is displayed in the status bar.

## Sorting results

By default the results are sorted by Name, then Path.

Sorting is reset back to the default each time the search parameters change.

At the top of the result list is a header. To sort a column click its header.

Note: Sorting can be slow when there are many results.

Sorting can be cancelled by selecting another sort or changing the search.

## Highlight the row the mouse is over

To highlight the row the mouse is over:

- In " _Everything_", from the **Tools** menu, click **Options**.
- Select the **View** tab.

{"answer":"- **What folder indexing is for:** Folder indexing allows Everything to include any folder in the Everything index, such as folders on local drives, external drives, network drives, network shares, cloud folders, and virtual folders. (Note: For FAT drives, the page mentions adding FAT and exFAT volumes directly through the FAT options page to avoid limitations where folder indexes can overwrite each other if assigned the same drive letter.)
- **How changes are picked up:** Everything monitors indexed folders for changes and also schedules a daily rescan of the indexed folders to detect changes that have been missed while Everything was not running.
- **Rescan options:**
  - Rescan an individual folder now via the **Index** menu -> **Rescan** submenu, or via **Tools** -> **Options** -> **Folders** tab -> **Rescan Now**.
  - Rescan all indexed folders now via the **Index** menu -> **Rescan** submenu -> **Rescan All**, or via **Tools** -> **Options** -> **Folders** tab -> **Rescan All Now**.
  - Scheduled options: Rescan every day or on a specific day at a specific time, rescan at a specific interval, or never rescan.
  - Optional settings include "Rescan on full buffer" and "Fast rescan" (which only works for NTFS folders).
- **Limits:**
  - Initial indexing can take a few minutes, and you cannot search the folder until it is complete.
  - Folder indexing is slower than native NTFS indexing.
  - If two different drives are assigned the same drive letter (such as `E:`), the folder index for one drive can overwrite the index for the other during a rescan.
  - Displaying icons and file information for offline folders can take several seconds to time out.
  - Mapped network drives and network shares are limited to a 64 KB change buffer size.
  - Fast rescan only works for NTFS folders; enabling it for other file systems may cause Everything to miss changes.
  - Mapped network drives are not available when running Everything as administrator.","metadata":{"author":"webhost2","title":"Folder Indexing - voidtools","viewport":"width=920","language":"en","favicon":"https://www.voidtools.com/favicon.ico","scrapeId":"01a19e95-ca65-718f-92bf-83e623e89345","sourceURL":"https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/folder_indexing/","url":"https://www.voidtools.com/support/everything/folder_indexing/","statusCode":200,"contentType":"text/html","proxyUsed":"basic","cacheState":"hit","cachedAt":"2026-11-02T09:34:30.233Z","creditsUsed":5,"concurrencyLimited":false}}
